row.Timeframe: 2026-09-10 onward; resolves when the fifth qualifying observation publishes, ceiling 2026-10-15 17:00 ET
row.Resolution_Criteria: BASIS NAMED PER WQ-162 FOR ALL FIVE OBSERVATIONS THE GRADE READS. SERIES: DFII10 (H.15 10-Year TIPS constant maturity, percent, daily business days). UNIT: percent to 2dp as published; the gate reads 2.50pct. VINTAGE: AS FIRST PUBLISHED. ** SESSION-SET DEFINITION, AND IT IS THE LOAD-BEARING CLAUSE: ** the five sessions are the first five for which FRED PUBLISHES a non-missing DFII10 observation with observation date >= 2026-09-10, taken in OBSERVATION-DATE order. Dates FRED never publishes are SKIPPED, not counted as misses. ** A PUBLICATION GAP MUST NOT BE ALLOWED TO DECIDE A MARKET QUESTION ** -- that is the precise failure this clause exists to prevent, and it is live, because the 2026-09-11 cell was still absent on the fourth day at registration. OPERATOR AND BOUNDARY: count the members closing >= 2.50 (INCLUSIVE; a close of exactly 2.50 counts toward the total). TRUE iff count >= 3. FALSE iff count <= 2. CONSECUTIVENESS: NONE IS REQUIRED -- deliberately, so that this row stays agnostic to whether Will sets the gate's 'sustained' at 3 sessions, 5 consecutive, or another number. RESET: not applicable. MECE: count is an integer 0-5, split at 3. RESIDUAL BRANCH: if fewer than five qualifying observations exist by 2026-10-15 17:00 ET, resolves VOID-INSUFFICIENT-PUBLICATION, never FALSE. ANCHOR TYPE: OBSERVATION-COUNT anchor (the fifth published session), NOT a calendar date -- chosen precisely because the calendar is unreliable here.
row.Outcome: TRUE. The first FOUR published DFII10 sessions with observation date >= 2026-09-10 ALL closed at or above 2.50pct: 2026-09-10 = 2.55, 2026-09-11 = 2.60, 2026-09-14 = 2.60, 2026-09-15 = 2.62 (FRED H.15 primary, cache-busted fredgraph.csv read 2026-09-17 ~08:2x ET; corroborated by monitors/boot_recompute.py the same minute, DFII10 2.62 [2026-09-15]). Count >= 3 is met at 4-of-4, so the verdict is decided whatever the fifth session (2026-09-16, unpublished at resolution) prints -- resolved on the fourth publication, not the fifth, because the letter's TRUE condition is already unreachable-to-falsify. Registered 70pct on the TRUE side ==> a HIT. WHAT IT SETTLES: the 2026-09-10 breach was PERSISTENT, not a spike -- the substance of the sustain question. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE: the gate's 'sustained' COUNT is still Will's (WQ-246); this row is an input to that ruling and a substitute for none. DIRECTION DISCLOSED AGAIN: a TRUE flatters this desk's real-rate reading; the 9/16 FOMC sat inside the window and the DOVISH SEP that the registration named as the threat to persistence arrived (median terminal 4.125) and did NOT pull real yields back -- TIP -0.38pct on 9/16 (vendor), the 9/16 DFII10 cell not yet published.
row.Notes: ** PARTIAL DETERMINATION DISCLOSED AT REGISTRATION, because hiding it would inflate the apparent skill: ** session 1 of the five is 2026-09-10 at 2.55, which is ALREADY IN THE SET and already counts. The row therefore starts 1-of-1 and the live question is whether 2 of the next 4 published sessions close >= 2.50. WHY 70: 9/10 is banked; 9/11 is INFERRED at ~2.62 by three independent instruments (^TNX +3.1bp, T10YIE -4bp implying real rose ~7bp more than nominal, TIP -0.46pct vs IEF -0.19pct) -- BUT AN INFERENCE IS NOT A PRINT AND IS NOT COUNTED BY THIS RESOLVER, in either direction, which is the same rule this desk applied on 9/10 when the estimate pointed the other way. Against that: the 2026-09-16 FOMC sits INSIDE the window, and per KB-BND-283 a dovish SEP is precisely the event that would pull real yields back below 2.50 -- so three of the five remaining slots are exposed to a live event whose asymmetry this desk has argued runs the wrong way for persistence. One confirmed, one strongly indicated, three exposed. DIRECTION DISCLOSED: a TRUE supports this desk's real-rate-stress regime reading, so the asymmetric error to guard is a too-eager TRUE. ** THIS ROW SETS NO THRESHOLD AND DOES NOT PRE-EMPT WQ-246: ** it reports how many of five sessions held the level, which is an input to any count Will chooses and a substitute for none.
row.If_Falsified_Action: If FALSE (2 or fewer of the first five published sessions close >= 2.50): the 2026-09-10 breach was a SPIKE, not a regime. Say that plainly against KB-BND-276 rather than treating a failed sustain as thesis-neutral -- it is evidence that the policy-path repricing OVERSHOT and mean-reverted, which weakens the real-rate-stress reading that this desk's long-end thesis leans on. Consequences: (1) record the count and the individual closes with dates; (2) notify TERRY, because the card's LEVEL letter fired on a move that did not hold, which is materially relevant to how that card's add line should be read next time; (3) feed the result to WQ-246 as evidence about what a sensible 'sustained' count would have to survive; (4) do NOT re-arm the gate at a lower level.
